title: Harmonic priority eviction and staged soft-degradation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a composable load-shedding mechanism that protects tenant SLOs during multi-region incidents and capacity shortfalls by combining a harmonic-priority eviction algorithm, admission control, and staged graceful-degradation modes. This ticket produces a playbook, implementation plan, and initial runtime prototype for Canary.

Motivation: Recent spikes in multi-region failover events highlighted that our current mitigation (simple token-bucket + model fallback) protects p50 at the expense of unbounded p95/p99 regressions and opaque tenant fairness. We need a predictable, observable, and auditable stack that: 1) preserves critical SLAs for high-tier customers, 2) gracefully degrades lower-priority workloads, and 3) allows operators to reason about end-user quality loss.

Proposal summary:
- Harmonic priority eviction: an eviction score that combines tenant weight, request recency, and estimated utility (SLO tier, active session count) via a harmonic mean to avoid domination by any single metric; eviction probability derived from score percentile within the shard.
- Admission control shim: lightweight pre-routing gate that computes per-request admission hints (cost estimate, deadline, tenant tier) and consults an adaptive policy (token buckets + soft credits) to either accept, queue, or apply a degradation token.
- Staged soft-degradation ladder: three ordered degradations applied as load increases: (1) Non-essential trimming (response length/metadata compression), (2) Partial generation / prefix-only responses + prefer cached answers, (3) Model-fallback to smaller quantized variant or sampling with reduced max_tokens. Each stage has a target SLO impact budget.
- Circuit-breaker integration: integrate shard-level circuit state (closed, probed, open) so admission control gradually tightens during open windows and automatically relaxes on probe success.
- Observability: per-tenant impact metrics (degradations_applied, fraction_accepted, p95_latency, quality_regressions) surfaced in Console with rollout toggles and historic incident views.

Non-goals: full rework of scheduler; replacing KV cache policy; end-user UX for degradation messaging (handled by product later).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Design doc reviewed and approved by infra and runtime leads; 2) Prototype integrated into 1 region Canary that can enable/disable harmonic eviction via feature flag; 3) Benchmarks showing p99 improvement for P0 tenants under synthetic overload while showing controlled quality loss for P3 tenants; 4) Console dashboard with per-tenant degradation counters and a basic playbook page; 5) Automated unit tests for eviction scoring and admission gate logic.
implementation_notes:
Implementation plan in three phases: Phase A (design + simulation): implement eviction score simulator using historical traces and produce heatmap of expected evictions per tenant over 30-day windows. Phase B (runtime shim): add admission control hook in front of router that computes admission hint and consults policy; expose feature flag and sampling endpoint. Phase C (rollout): canary in us-west-2, monitor dashboards, promote to multi-region with coordinated rollouts and fail-open policy.

Key data structures: compact per-tenant credit ledger, sliding-window recency counters, percentile sketch for eviction thresholds. Keep memory bounded per-shard (configurable retention).

Trade-offs considered: deterministic strict priority queues cause starvation; pure probabilistic shedding causes noisy regressions. The harmonic mean balances these by dampening extreme signals (e.g., a very active low-weight tenant won't monopolize). We accept slightly higher implementation complexity for measurability and smoother customer experience.
risks:
- Miscalibrated scoring could unintentionally evict mid-tier customers; mitigation: phased simulation and synthetic traffic tests.
- Added CPU/latency overhead at admission path; mitigation: keep gate path in C++ hot path and benchmark budget <2% p95.
- Complexity in multi-region coordination during failover; mitigation: central policy controller with conservative defaults and region-local fast-path.
- Quality regressions when stepping down models; mitigation: automatic A/B evaluation against small prompt sets and rollbacks.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for score math, percentile eviction, and admission decisions.
- Replay tests with 7-day traces in staging to validate eviction distribution and tenant fairness.
- Load test with synthetic tenant mix (10% P0, 30% P1, 60% P2/P3) and spike scenarios: sudden 3x traffic, region outage failover.
- Canary followed by progressive ramp: 1%, 5%, 25% with kill switches.
notes:
Design review 2026-03-02: infra requested a simpler fallback policy for first rollouts; runtime prefers tight memory bounds on tenant ledgers. Action: ship Phase A sim and a limited-feature Phase B without percentile sketches.

Open questions: how to encode per-request estimated utility for composite API calls (embedding+generate); whether to surface degradation level in response headers for downstream routing.
